thesis: ZIM's confirmed second-quarter release supports a long: revenue increased 9% year over year, net income increased to $64 million, and free cash flow was $386 million; the issuer identifies IFRS as its reporting framework. The strongest counter-evidence is that first-half adjusted operating measures declined year over year and the signed Hapag-Lloyd transaction still depends on multiple regulatory approvals. Those risks keep conviction below high, but they do not overturn the positive read because second-quarter profitability improved, full-year adjusted operating guidance was maintained, and both parties continue to pursue the disclosed transaction.
invalidation: Invalidate the long if ZIM withdraws or materially reduces its full-year operating guidance, reports a renewed material deterioration in freight economics, or discloses that the signed Hapag-Lloyd transaction is terminated or materially less likely to close.

thesis: Aveanna's confirmed second-quarter results support a long: revenue increased 13.7% year over year to $670.5 million, net income increased to $40.3 million, and the company raised full-year revenue and adjusted operating guidance. The strongest counter-evidence is substantial reimbursement and leverage exposure plus a recent large secondary sale by existing holders. It does not overturn the read because the operating improvement covered all three segments, management raised guidance after the quarter, and the company explicitly stated that it issued no shares and received no proceeds in the secondary offering, so that transaction was not issuer dilution.
invalidation: Invalidate the long if Aveanna cuts its revised 2026 revenue or adjusted operating guidance, reports renewed margin deterioration, or discloses a material adverse reimbursement change that undermines the current operating trajectory.

thesis: Royalty Pharma's September 4 company disclosure supports avoiding a new entry: the Phase 3 HORIZON trial for pelacarsen did not meet its primary cardiovascular endpoint, removing a development-stage source of upside. The strongest positive counter-evidence is the protective Spinraza-linked funding structure, which management expects will recoup the total investment with a modest positive return, alongside reiterated long-term Portfolio Receipts goals. That protection does not reverse the avoid read because a modest contractual return replaces the failed program's royalty upside and complete trial data remain pending.
invalidation: Reverse the avoid thesis if independently presented HORIZON data establish a commercially meaningful path for pelacarsen, or a subsequent issuer update replaces the lost upside with a comparably de-risked and material source of Portfolio Receipts while maintaining current guidance.

thesis: Aehr's confirmed $22 million follow-on order for AI-processor wafer-level burn-in systems supports a long, reinforced by $100.6 million of effective backlog disclosed with fiscal-year results. The strongest counter-evidence is that fiscal 2026 revenue declined to $50.0 million from $59.0 million and the annual net loss widened, showing that the growth narrative has not yet translated into full-year profitability. It does not overturn the read because the signed follow-on order and record backlog are already disclosed customer commitments rather than a technical or sector-only signal, although fiscal 2027 guidance remains forward-looking.
invalidation: Invalidate the long if Aehr reports cancellation or material delay of the disclosed AI order, effective backlog falls materially without conversion to revenue, or fiscal 2027 revenue guidance is reduced below its current range.
sources: Aehr fiscal 2026 fourth-quarter and full-year results: https://www.aehr.com/2026/07/aehr-test-systems-reports-fiscal-2026-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-financial-results-with-record-quarterly-bookings-and-100-million-effective-backlog/

thesis: The held BOXX position still supports a long: the issuer describes the fund as an options-based alternative to an ultrashort-duration bond position, and its September 4 disclosures showed market price close to NAV with a one-cent 30-day median bid-ask spread. The strongest counter-evidence is that the near-52-week-high signal is largely mechanical accrual tied to short-term rates rather than a company-specific catalyst, while box-spread execution and tax treatment remain structural risks. The tight disclosed market-to-NAV relationship and unchanged strategy support continuing to hold, but the mechanical and macro-linked nature of the return forces low conviction.
invalidation: Exit the thesis if the fund develops a sustained material premium or discount to NAV, its bid-ask spread widens materially, or a prospectus or regulatory change alters the box-spread strategy or its expected ultrashort-duration behavior.
sources: Alpha Architect BOXX fund page: https://funds.alphaarchitect.com/boxetf/
